summary.short: Amends the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) and two other regulations to simplify its implementation. Adds prohibitions on AI systems generating non-consensual intimate or child sexual abuse material, sets high-risk application dates of 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028, and changes conformity assessment, sandbox and AI Office rules.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amends the AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the civil aviation regulation (EU) 2018/1139 and the machinery regulation (EU) 2023/1230 to simplify AI Act implementation. It narrows the safety component definition, adds SME and small mid-cap definitions, and replaces the AI literacy duty with a duty to take measures to support AI literacy. A new Article 4a permits providers and deployers, under listed conditions, to process special categories of personal data for bias detection and correction. Article 5 adds prohibitions on placing on the market, putting into service or using AI systems that generate non-consensual intimate material or child sexual abuse material, with limits for providers and deployers, applicable from 2 December 2026. High-risk rules in Chapter III, Sections 1 to 3 apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I systems. The text changes conformity assessment and notified body designation (single application procedure), sandbox and real-world testing rules, quality management and documentation simplifications for SMEs and SMCs, and AI Office supervision, investigation, administrative fines and periodic penalty payments (Articles 75 to 75d). Machinery moves from Section A to Section B of Annex I. Article 4 sets entry into force on the third day after publication.

obligations.summary: AI Office shall be allocated adequate resources to perform its duties and exercise its powers under the Regulation, without prejudice to the budgetary procedure.
obligations.conditional_on: Without prejudice to the budgetary procedure

evidence.quote: the AI Office shall be allocated adequate resources to effectively perform its duties

obligations.summary: Member States may be required to pay fees to experts of the scientific panel for advice and support, at a rate equivalent to Commission remuneration.
obligations.conditional_on: Where Member States call upon the scientific panel's expertise

evidence.quote: The Member States may be required to pay fees for the advice and support provided by the experts

obligations.summary: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on implementation, in particular to SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs, taking into account Board and Commission guidance.

evidence.quote: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on the implementation of this Regulation

obligations.summary: Where guidance concerns AI systems in areas covered by other Union law, the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted, as appropriate.
obligations.conditional_on: Where guidance on an AI system in areas covered by other Union law is intended

evidence.quote: the national competent authorities under that Union law shall be consulted, as appropriate

obligations.summary: The post-market monitoring system of high-risk AI system providers shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan forming part of the Annex IV technical documentation.

evidence.provision: Art. 1(30) (replacing Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 Art. 72(3), first and second sentences)
evidence.quote: The post-market monitoring system shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan.

obligations.summary: Commission, taking utmost account of the Board opinion, shall adopt guidance including a template on the post-market monitoring plan.

evidence.quote: The Commission, taking utmost account of the opinion of the Board, shall adopt guidance, including a template, on the post-market monitoring plan by 2 September 2027.

obligations.summary: AI Office is exclusively competent for supervision and enforcement regarding AI systems based on general-purpose AI models of the same undertaking and AI systems in or integrated into very large online platforms or search engines; it conducts conformity assessments and tests of certain high-risk systems, notifies the national market surveillance authority before restricting or withdrawing a system, and transmits incident information to the national authority.
obligations.conditional_on: Subject to the exceptions in Art. 75(1)(a)(i) to (iv)

evidence.quote: The AI Office shall be exclusively competent for the supervision and enforcement of the obligations under this Regulation

obligations.summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems under AI Office competence shall report serious incidents to the AI Office, with Art. 73(2) to (9) applying mutatis mutandis.
obligations.conditional_on: High-risk AI systems subject to AI Office competence under Art. 75(1)

evidence.quote: providers of high-risk AI systems subject to the competence of the AI Office pursuant to paragraph 1 of this Article shall report any serious incidents to the AI Office

obligations.summary: Authorities involved in applying the Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide necessary assistance for its powers, including inspections in Member States.

evidence.quote: The authorities involved in the application of this Regulation shall cooperate actively with the AI Office

obligations.summary: Provider of a high-risk AI system that applied for third-party conformity assessment by the Commission shall pay fees and, for costs of services entrusted to notified bodies, pay the notified body directly.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the provider has applied for a third-party conformity assessment under Art. 75(1e)

evidence.quote: The provider shall pay the costs related to the services entrusted by the Commission to the notified bodies

obligations.summary: A market surveillance authority with well-founded reasons to suspect an infringement shall cooperate actively with the AI Office and provide assistance for its powers when it requests assessment of a matter.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the market surveillance authority requests the AI Office to assess a matter

evidence.quote: the market surveillance authority shall cooperate actively and provide the AI Office the necessary assistance

obligations.summary: AI Office shall take utmost account of a market surveillance authority request and inform the single point of contact of its intention to exercise powers under Art. 75a or its reasons for not exercising them; if it exercises them it shall periodically inform the single point of contact of major developments.
obligations.applies_from: no later than four months following receipt of the request
obligations.conditional_on: Where a market surveillance authority submits a request under Art. 75(2a)

evidence.quote: The AI Office shall, without undue delay and in any event no later than four months following receipt of the request, inform the single point of contact

obligations.summary: When requesting information, the AI Office shall state the legal basis and purpose, specify the information required and set a period; for voluntary replies it shall indicate that information must be correct and not misleading. It shall notify the operator when starting an investigation, inform the provider before inspections, and use information collected only for the Regulation's purposes.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the AI Office exercises its powers under Art. 75a

evidence.quote: When requesting information, the AI Office shall state the legal basis and the purpose of the request

obligations.summary: Where the AI Office considers that an operator's commitments cannot ensure effective compliance, it shall reject them in a reasoned decision when concluding proceedings.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the operator has offered commitments under Art. 75b

evidence.quote: it shall reject those commitments in a reasoned decision when concluding the proceedings

obligations.summary: AI Office shall adopt a decision establishing non-compliance, communicate preliminary findings to the operator before deciding, order measures within a reasonable period where relevant, and close proceedings by decision where no grounds exist. Penalty provisions in Art. 75c(4) to (8) are excluded.
obligations.conditional_on: Where the AI Office finds non-compliance

evidence.quote: Before adopting a decision pursuant to paragraph 1, the AI Office shall communicate its preliminary findings to the operator concerned

obligations.summary: AI Office shall fully respect the rights of defence and access to the file of operators in proceedings, and shall publish the decisions it adopts under Art. 75b and 75c, stating the parties and main content.

evidence.quote: The rights of defence and of access to the file of operators falling within the scope of Article 75(1) shall be fully respected in proceedings.

obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities shall grant public authorities protecting fundamental rights access to information or documentation held under the Regulation, including by requesting it from providers or deployers where necessary and without undue delay.
obligations.conditional_on: Where access is necessary for the public authority to fulfil its mandate

evidence.quote: the market surveillance authority shall grant the relevant public authority or body referred to in paragraph 1 access

obligations.summary: Market surveillance authorities and public authorities protecting fundamental rights shall cooperate closely and provide mutual assistance, including exchange of information, for coherent application of the Regulation.

evidence.quote: Market surveillance authorities and public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 shall cooperate closely

obligations.summary: AI Office and Member States shall take into account the specific interests and needs of SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs when encouraging and facilitating codes of conduct.

evidence.quote: The AI Office and the Member States shall take into account the specific interests and needs of SMEs

obligations.summary: Commission shall publish guidelines on practical implementation of Art. 8(2), 9(10) and 17(3) for complementarity and proportionality with Annex I legislation, involving the Board and paying attention to SMEs, SMCs, local public authorities and affected sectors.

evidence.quote: such guidelines shall be published by 1 August 2027

obligations.summary: Power to adopt delegated acts under Art. 2(13) and Art. 30(2) is conferred on the Commission for five years, tacitly extendable, revocable by Parliament or Council.

evidence.quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 2(13) and Article 30(2) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 27 July 2026

obligations.summary: Commission shall draw up a report on the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period.

evidence.quote: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period

obligations.summary: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended for use by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply with the Regulation, for systems placed on the market or put into service before the application date of Chapter III and only if significantly changed.
obligations.conditional_on: Systems placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III, subject to significant changes in design

evidence.quote: the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply

obligations.summary: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content and placed on the market before 2 August 2026 shall take the necessary steps to comply with Art. 50(2).
obligations.conditional_on: Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026

evidence.quote: shall take the necessary steps in order to comply with Article 50(2) by 2 December 2026

obligations.summary: Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and types of AI systems in Annex XIV when specifying the types of AI systems in the application for designation under Art. 29.

evidence.quote: Conformity assessment bodies shall use the lists of codes, categories and corresponding types of AI systems set out in this Annex

obligations.summary: Under amended Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, when the Commission adopts implementing or delegated acts on AI safety components (Arts 27, 31, 32, 36, 39, 50 and 53), it shall take into account the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
obligations.conditional_on: When adopting implementing or delegated acts concerning AI systems that are safety components

evidence.quote: the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2, of that Regulation shall be taken into account.

obligations.summary: Commission shall adopt delegated acts under Art. 47 to amend Annex III of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 by adding health and safety requirements for high-risk AI systems that are safety components in machinery or are machinery, reflecting Chapter III, Section 2 and Articles 17, 19, 72 and 73 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies to AI systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 due to being a safety component in a product covered by Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

evidence.quote: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 47 of this Regulation to amend Annex III

enforcement.triggered_by: Infringement of any applicable provision of this Regulation, including those not listed in Art. 99(4); failure to comply with decisions or measures under Art. 14(4) or 16(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 or Art. 75a; failure to comply with a commitment made binding under Art. 75b
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Subject to administrative fines as referred to in Art. 99(4); the amount is not stated in this text
enforcement.penalty_formula: Amounts are set in Art. 99(4), which this text does not state. Art. 99(3) to (7) apply mutatis mutandis to AI Office penalties (Art. 75c(4)).

evidence.quote: In particular, the following shall be subject to administrative fines as referred to in Article 99(4):

enforcement.triggered_by: Supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to the AI Office in reply to a request
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Subject to administrative fines as referred to in Art. 99(5); the amount is not stated in this text
enforcement.penalty_formula: Amount is set in Art. 99(5), which this text does not state.

evidence.quote: The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to the AI Office in reply to a request shall be subject to administrative fines as referred to in Article 99(5).

enforcement.triggered_by: Failure to comply with the obligations listed in Art. 75c(5)(a) to (g), including submitting to an investigation or inspection, complying with an information request, corrective actions, binding commitments, or a decision under Art. 75c(1)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Periodic penalty payments shall not exceed 5 % of the average daily income or worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year per day, where applicable
enforcement.penalty_formula: Up to 5 % of average daily income or worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, per day, calculated from the date appointed by the decision

evidence.quote: shall not exceed 5 % of the average daily income or worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year per day

enforcement.triggered_by: Any infringement of this Regulation by operators; Member States' rules may include administrative fines, warnings and non-monetary measures
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Member States lay down the penalty rules; no amount is stated in this text. For SMCs, each fine under Art. 99(4) and (5) is up to the percentages or amount referred to there, whichever is lower (Art. 99(6a))
enforcement.penalty_formula: For SMCs, each fine referred to in Art. 99(4) and (5) is up to the percentages or amount referred therein, whichever is lower (Art. 99(6a), inserted by Art. 1(38)(c)).

evidence.quote: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures, which may also include administrative fines, warnings and non-monetary measures

enforcement.authority: Not stated specifically in this text for Art. 99(4) (Member State penalty rules under Art. 99(1))
enforcement.triggered_by: Infringement of the obligations of providers and operators under Art. 25(2) and (4), added to the list in Art. 99(4)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Amount set in Art. 99(4); not stated in this text
enforcement.penalty_formula: Amount is set in Art. 99(4), which this text does not state; SMC cap per Art. 99(6a).

evidence.quote: obligations of providers and operators pursuant to Article 25(2) and (4)

enforcement.authority: AI Office (must notify the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned before deciding)
enforcement.triggered_by: A decision that would have the effect of prohibiting or restricting an AI system being made available or put into service on a national market, or a decision to withdraw or recall the AI system from such market
enforcement.max_penalty_text: No penalty amount; a market measure

evidence.quote: a decision to withdraw or recall the AI system from such market

enforcement.triggered_by: A decision establishing non-compliance by an operator under Art. 75c(1)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Corrective order to take the necessary measures within a reasonable period specified in the decision; no penalty amount
enforcement.cure_period: A reasonable period specified in the decision (Art. 75c(3)); length not stated

evidence.quote: order the operator concerned to take the necessary measures to ensure compliance with the relevant provisions of this Regulation within a reasonable period specified therein

enforcement.triggered_by: Instances of non-compliance with this Regulation by an operator under the AI Office's supervision and enforcement
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Full reclaim of the costs of supervision and enforcement activities from the relevant operator; no amount stated
enforcement.penalty_formula: Costs of supervision and enforcement activities, including human and technical resources (Art. 75a(1), referring to Art. 15 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020)

evidence.quote: The AI Office shall be authorised to fully reclaim from the relevant operator the totality of the costs of its supervision and enforcement activities with respect to instances of non-compliance
